name: Set and Forget on BTC and ETH 1H

sections.hypothesis: On BTC and ETH, buying a 1H bullish engulfing candle inside a 4H demand zone touched at least three times, while the weekly and daily structure are both rising, with a stop below the zone and a 3R target, beats random entries with the same stops, targets and sizing, and beats holding at the same exposure on Sharpe, after costs.
sections.rationale: Who pays, as the method claims (Alex, 'Set and Forget', Luke's YouTube batch 1 S1, forex in the original): a level that has held several times holds resting buy orders, and in an uptrend late sellers into it are absorbed. The original draws its zones by eye; this note makes them mechanical (clusters of 4H swing lows), so it tests a coded cousin, not the trader's judgement. Against it, honestly: it is the chart-pattern and level family, which the entry bar names as rejected; Kestrel's level retest, trendline, wedge and structure-pullback tests all failed. Freezing this note is Luke's knowing override (2026-11-16).
sections.rules: set-and-forget, BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT 1H separately, spot, long only. Higher timeframes are built from the 1H bars (4H from 00:00 UTC, daily, weekly from Monday 00:00 UTC); a higher-timeframe bar is used only once it has closed. Swings: a bar whose high is above the 3 bars before it and at least the 3 after it (lows mirrored), known once the last of those has closed. Bias: on the weekly and on the daily, the last two known swing highs and the last two known swing lows are both rising. Zones: 4H swing lows known by now from the last 90 days; a zone is a band no wider than 0.5 x daily ATR(14) holding at least 3 of them, from the lowest to the highest of those lows. Entry: while the bias is up, a 1H bullish engulfing (prior bar down; this bar opens at or below its close and closes above its open) whose low is inside a zone and whose close is above the zone's bottom (inside several zones: the lowest zone's bottom). Buy at the next open; stop at the zone's bottom less 0.1 x daily ATR(14); target 3R from the signal close. One trade at a time. Costs from kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee a side, 1 bp half-spread: a 17 bps round trip), 330 USDT, 1% risk per trade sized by the engine, capped at 100% of equity. Period 2020-01 to 2025-10, before the holdout.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard on each coin, including test 9 (beat 95% of 200 random-entry paths with the same stops, targets and sizing). Fails if neither coin passes every test.
sections.parameters: swing_bars 3 (2-5), touches 3 (2-5), zone_atr_tenths 5 (2-10, i.e. 0.2-1 x daily ATR), lookback_days 90 (30-180), target_r 3 (2-4). One setting on each coin: 2 runs; the robustness check moves each (about 20 neighbours a coin).
sections.costs: 1H entries with zone stops, perhaps 1-3% away: a 17 bps round trip is about 0.05-0.15R a trade, so costs matter far less than on 5m. The rule signals about 40 times a year a coin (215 on BTC and 240 on ETH in 2020-25, counted from signals, not outcomes); fewer fills, since one trade is held at a time. Trials: 2 runs plus about 40 neighbours; random-entry paths aren't trials.

history.reason: FAIL, rejected with Luke's say-so (2026-11-16). Fails test 1 on both coins, 1H 2020-01 to 2025-10: BTC +0.6% (Sharpe 0.04) against +12% for BTC held at the same exposure, 62 trades, +0.02R a trade, break-even 19 bps vs 17 (2x needed); ETH -6.2% (Sharpe -0.18) against +15%, 59 trades, -0.09R. Costs were small (0.06-0.07R): the mechanical version of the method has no edge before costs. Robustness not run (Luke).
